text.arabic_uthmani: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَهُمْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يُقْضَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا۟ وَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُم مِّنْ عَذَابِهَا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى كُلَّ كَفُورٍۢ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that resumes from the saved scene while introducing the condemned class

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: relative pronoun introducing the condemned class

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens 35:36 as a connected contrast, not as a loose list marker. It carries the listener out of the protected testimony of 35:34-35 and attaches the turn to {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}), so the boundary and the new class arrive in one bound move. The payoff is a sharp reversal with audible continuity: double safety before, double non-relief here.

topics.headline: coordinated scene boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the new sentence is linked to the prior blessed scene while separated from it as a contrasting class-frame.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction is locally licensed as coordination/resumption before the relative pronoun.

topics.headline: bound transition into class marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that transition is fused to the relative class marker rather than floating as an abstract discourse sign.
topics.reason: The particle is prefixed to the relative pronoun in the surface form.

topics.headline: audible reversal from safety to non-relief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the previous double protection inverted into the condemned group's double denial of relief.
topics.reason: The discourse and cadence rows connect the ayah boundary to the later paired negations.

words.gloss_range: definite relative pronoun whose class is completed by the following denial verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: perfect plural denial verb defining the class

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not name a group by ancestry or location; it waits for {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) to define the class by conduct. That delay matters because the fire is not introduced first: the sentence makes culpable action the doorway into the whole punishment scene. The final singular type in {{ar:كَفُورٍۢ}} ({{tr:kafūrin}}) will generalize what this opening relative frame first identifies.

topics.headline: relative class completed by conduct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punished group formed by a following act, not by a static label.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun requires its following clause before the predicate can be assigned.

topics.headline: relative form not ordinary definite noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the article-like surface is a frozen relative pronoun needing a clause.
topics.reason: The form functions pronominally rather than as a standalone definite noun.

topics.headline: third-person judgment scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the speech scene give way to a third-person judicial frame.
topics.reason: Context rows mark the move from saved testimony to condemned classification.

words.gloss_range: settled covering-denial without an explicit object, locally moving toward culpable ingratitude
words.root_gloss_range: broad covering, concealing, denial, expiation, and ingratitude field; local context selects culpable covering-denial answered by recompense
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) presents denial as an already settled plural act and leaves its object unstated, so signs, truth, benefaction, and obligation are not prematurely narrowed. The root field of covering becomes visible when the consequence is exposed as {{ar:نَارُ}} ({{tr:nāru}}): what was covered is answered by manifest fire. The ayah also frames a bookend, moving from this plural act to the intensive closing type {{ar:كَفُورٍۢ}} ({{tr:kafūrin}}).

topics.headline: settled objectless denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the blame is established before punishment is named and is not limited to one omitted object.
topics.reason: The perfect plural verb is the relative clause, and no direct object is supplied.

topics.headline: covering-denial selected locally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the physical covering image become moral concealment exposed by fire, while unrelated branches do not replace the local denial sense.
topics.reason: V4-style root range supports covering and denial, but local punishment and closing intensive form select culpable denial/ingratitude.

topics.headline: opening act to closing type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah convert an opening plural act into a final character category.
topics.reason: Inter, echo, and structure rows tie the first k-f-r verb to the closing intensive noun and to recompense.

words.gloss_range: prefixed lām of adverse allotment before the fire is named
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the allotment marker inside {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}); it makes assignment to the condemned group the first pressure of the predicate. The fire is not merely described somewhere in the scene; it accrues to them as an adverse due before {{ar:نَارُ}} ({{tr:nāru}}) is spoken. The fronted phrase therefore makes restriction and allocation work together.

topics.headline: fronted adverse allotment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sentence first assigns the outcome to them and only afterward names the fire.
topics.reason: The lām phrase is fronted as the nominal predicate with the following fire as delayed subject/core.

topics.headline: bound lām plus pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees adverse possession compressed into one surface unit with the pronoun.
topics.reason: The preposition is prefixed to the following pronoun and governs it.

topics.headline: clipped allocation formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the punishment as a terse allocation formula rather than a loose description.
topics.reason: The fronting and omitted copular relation compact the nominal clause.

words.gloss_range: third masculine plural suffix anchoring the same condemned group through the punishment sequence
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) in {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) routes the fire back to the relative group and begins the suffix chain continued by {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) and {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}). The same plural target is assigned fire, held under non-completion, and denied removal. That continuity makes the punishment one closed referential state, not three disconnected clauses.

topics.headline: same group through suffix chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one condemned group through allotment, imposed non-completion, and denied removal.
topics.reason: The same third masculine plural suffix recurs across the prepositional phrases.

topics.headline: definite bound pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fire is assigned to the already identified relative group before later generalization.
topics.reason: The suffix is definite and bound to the preposition.

topics.headline: protected self-report to exposed liability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior saved first-person voice replaced by third-person liability.
topics.reason: Context rows contrast the prior speech register with this objective verdict register.

words.gloss_range: specified fire-domain as the assigned outcome, not generic flame or guidance-light
words.root_gloss_range: broad fire/light field; local construct selects concrete punitive fire, not guidance-light
words.prose: {{ar:نَارُ}} ({{tr:nāru}}) lands after {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}), so the fire is heard as the assigned payload of the predicate. Its construct link to {{ar:جَهَنَّمَ}} ({{tr:jahannama}}) makes it a specified domain, and the later suffix in {{ar:عَذَابِهَا}} ({{tr:ʿadhābihā}}) treats that domain as owning torment. The n-w-r field is narrowed here to burning exposure, not guiding light (24:35); even the visible signal or campfire image is inverted into an announcement of liability rather than hospitality.

topics.headline: construct fire-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the allotted outcome as a named fire-domain rather than generic flame.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative in construct with the proper name that specifies it.

topics.headline: fire pole over light pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root field shift from illumination to exposing blaze, while the local noun blocks a guidance-light reading.
topics.reason: The noun selects concrete fire; cross-passage light contrast is useful but not locally governing.

topics.headline: domain before no-exit clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the non-death and non-lightening clauses occur inside an already named punitive environment.
topics.reason: The fire-domain is established before the two negated passive blocks and is recalled by the feminine suffix.

words.gloss_range: proper name specifying the fire as Jahannam-domain
words.root_gloss_range: foreign proper-name behavior limits native derivational root play; locally it names the punitive domain

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: feminine suffix referring back to the fire-domain

words.prose: {{ar:جَهَنَّمَ}} ({{tr:jahannama}}) specifies {{ar:نَارُ}} ({{tr:nāru}}) as a proper named domain. Its fixed proper-name behavior matters: the word is not a native derivational play here but the place-name that encloses the following non-death and non-relief clauses. Against gate-and-apportioned-entry framing (15:44), this occurrence specializes the familiar domain as a no-death, no-reduction state. Because the later {{ar:هَا}} ({{tr:hā}}) in {{ar:عَذَابِهَا}} ({{tr:ʿadhābihā}}) points back to the fire-domain, the punishment remains domain-owned.

topics.headline: proper name in construct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the fire is specified by a named domain, not modified by an ordinary adjective.
topics.reason: The proper noun is governed by the construct head while retaining diptote-like surface behavior.

topics.headline: fixed domain name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader avoids forcing native root semantics and keeps the payoff on the named punitive domain.
topics.reason: The evidence treats the word as a foreign proper name, limiting productive Arabic derivation.

topics.headline: domain prepared for suffix return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the named domain becomes the antecedent complex for the later possessed punishment.
topics.reason: Structural rows connect the construct phrase to the feminine suffix in the punishment phrase.

words.gloss_range: first negative particle denying the completion event whose result would be death
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) scopes over {{ar:يُقْضَىٰ}} ({{tr:yuqḍā}}), not directly over {{ar:يَمُوتُوا۟}} ({{tr:yamūtū}}). That makes non-death depend on a prior blocked completion: the death result cannot arrive because the completing verdict is denied. The repeated negative architecture begins here and will be balanced by the second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) before mitigation.

topics.headline: negation over completion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees death blocked through the denial of completion rather than by a separate death-negation formula.
topics.reason: The first negative particle governs the passive imperfect completion verb.

topics.headline: visible separate negator
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices polarity and verbal process as distinct visible pieces.
topics.reason: The particle remains separate before the following verb.

topics.headline: first half of double denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first negative block set up the ayah's paired impossibilities.
topics.reason: The first negative clause is coordinated later with a second negative passive clause.

words.gloss_range: negated passive completion/decree imposed upon them, with death as the withheld endpoint
words.root_gloss_range: judging, decreeing, settling, completing, and finishing; local passive under negation selects withheld terminal settlement

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negative particle in the first denial

words.prose: {{ar:يُقْضَىٰ}} ({{tr:yuqḍā}}) carries q-d-y as completion and verdict at once. Under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) and with {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}), it imagines final settlement as something that would fall upon them, then denies it; {{ar:فَيَمُوتُوا۟}} ({{tr:fa-yamūtū}}) reveals that the withheld settlement would have been death. That reversal contrasts with settled-matter language in 19:21, where the same root marks completed settledness, while the passive form and active-like variant make voice a pressure point. The passive keeps the sufferers foregrounded until {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) later reintroduces active recompensing agency.

topics.headline: passive completion denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees death denied as withheld final settlement, not just as one missing event.
topics.reason: The negated passive imperfect governs the following result clause and takes the affected party with upon-preposition.

topics.headline: judgment and completion pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices legal verdict and existential closure converging locally, while broader q-d-y uses remain outside the selected frame.
topics.reason: Root evidence supports judgment/completion; local death-result syntax selects terminal settlement.

topics.headline: passive state before active recompense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the passive suffering clauses later resolved as administered recompense rather than impersonal mechanics.
topics.reason: The word participates in the paired passive clauses before the active closing verb.

words.gloss_range: upon-them complement marking imposed verdict over the same plural target
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) makes the denied completion a verdict that would come upon the condemned group. The same suffix heard in {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) remains the target, while the preposition changes the relation from allotment to imposed burden. Its later counterpart {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) reverses direction, so nothing comes upon them to finish the punishment and nothing lifts away from them to ease it.

topics.headline: same target under imposed verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same plural group from assigned fire into the denied imposed completion.
topics.reason: The suffix agrees with the prior group and the phrase complements the passive completion verb.

topics.headline: upon and away-from opposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees spatial logic intensify the trap: imposed finality is denied, then removal is denied.
topics.reason: The upon-preposition contrasts with the later away-from-preposition while keeping the same suffix.

topics.headline: bound burden phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears burden and target compressed into a single surface phrase.
topics.reason: The preposition and suffix are fused in one word.

words.gloss_range: result particle making death dependent on the denied completion
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the result hinge before {{ar:يَمُوتُوا۟}} ({{tr:yamūtū}}). It does not merely move the sentence forward; it makes death the consequence that would follow if {{ar:يُقْضَىٰ}} ({{tr:yuqḍā}}) occurred. Since the completion is negated, the attached result particle traps death as an unrealized outcome.

topics.headline: result relation to denied completion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees death subordinated to the completion clause instead of standing as an independent second event.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the result clause after the negated passive completion clause.

topics.headline: bound result marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that causal dependency is visible in the word shape attached to the death verb.
topics.reason: The particle is prefixed to the following verb.

topics.headline: death as unrealized output
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first negation disable the expected terminal result.
topics.reason: Structure rows tie the particle to the blocked pathway from completion to death.

words.gloss_range: death as the dependent endpoint that would end torment but is withheld
words.root_gloss_range: death, cessation, stillness, lifelessness, and extinguishing; local syntax selects death as denied relief/endpoint

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: result particle before the death verb

words.prose: {{ar:يَمُوتُوا۟}} ({{tr:yamūtū}}) names the endpoint that would have followed completed judgment, but its mood and placement after {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) keep it dependent and unrealized. Locally, death is not the punishment itself; it is the cessation that would end sensation, and that relief is withheld. The abnormality is sharpened by the wider non-death formula in 20:74, while 35:36 gives the mechanism through denied completion.

topics.headline: dependent death result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar does not narrate dying; it bars death as a result that cannot materialize.
topics.reason: The verb lacks final nūn after result governance and shares the plural subject of the condemned group.

topics.headline: cessation as denied relief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees death inverted from feared loss into withheld relief, while broader death imagery remains subordinated to this local endpoint.
topics.reason: Root evidence supports cessation/stillness, and local no-exit syntax selects denied terminal relief.

topics.headline: non-death formula mechanism
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this dependent syntax with the broader no-death motif, especially 20:74, without making that passage govern the parse.
topics.reason: Inter rows use concrete references to show formulaic resonance and same-surah inversion.

words.gloss_range: coordinator adding the second negated passive block cumulatively

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negative particle in the first denial

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) before the second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) makes mitigation denial cumulative with death denial. The clause is not an alternative route; it is a second door closing after the first. Its bound surface in {{ar:وَلَا}} ({{tr:wa-lā}}) keeps the second negative panel visibly dependent on the first.

topics.headline: cumulative second denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees non-lightening added to non-death rather than substituted for it.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates a second negated passive clause with the first.

topics.headline: bound coordination to negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second barrier as a compact coordinated-negative unit.
topics.reason: The conjunction is prefixed to the following negator.

topics.headline: audible double-denial frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears two parallel closures: no completed death and no lightening of punishment.
topics.reason: Cadence and structure rows treat the two negatives as a balanced pair.

words.gloss_range: second negative particle opening a distinct mitigation denial
words.prose: The second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) does not restate the first; it scopes over {{ar:يُخَفَّفُ}} ({{tr:yukhaffafu}}) and opens a new blocked relief. After the endpoint has been denied, this particle denies reduction in intensity. Repetition of the same negator preserves the parallel architecture of the two central passive clauses.

topics.headline: new scope over mitigation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a fresh blocked relief after blocked death, not a mere repetition.
topics.reason: The second negative particle governs a different passive verb.

topics.headline: second coordinated barrier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices coordination and negation fused into the second gate of the structure.
topics.reason: The particle appears after the prefixed conjunction in a compact surface form.

topics.headline: parallel no-exit structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees endpoint and reduction barred in matching grammar.
topics.reason: The repeated negator helps construct the ayah's double negative architecture.

words.gloss_range: negated passive Form II lightening/reduction of punishment
words.root_gloss_range: lightness, easing, reduction, treating as slight; local Form II passive selects denied mitigation of a burden
words.prose: {{ar:يُخَفَّفُ}} ({{tr:yukhaffafu}}) turns punishment into a load or intensity that could have been lightened, then denies that relief. Its Form II passive keeps the reducer unnamed and focuses on non-occurrence of mitigation itself. With {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) and {{ar:مِّنْ عَذَابِهَا}} ({{tr:min ʿadhābihā}}), the grammar imagines relief lifted away from them and reduced from the punishment, then refuses both. Compared with no-lightening formulas such as 2:86, its placement after blocked death closes the weaker escape after the stronger endpoint has been refused.

topics.headline: passive mitigation denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second block deny any act of relief, not merely report that relief is absent once.
topics.reason: The passive imperfect under negation is coordinated with the earlier passive completion clause.

topics.headline: punishment as unlightened load
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment construed as burden or intensity, while unrelated lightness uses stay outside the local mitigation frame.
topics.reason: Root and Form II evidence support making-light/reduction; local complements select punishment mitigation.

topics.headline: mitigation after terminal exit denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a weaker escape closed after death itself has been blocked.
topics.reason: The clause follows the death result and participates in recurring no-lightening formulas such as 2:86.

words.gloss_range: away-from-them complement marking denied removal of punishment from the same group
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) gives lightening a removal direction: punishment would be moved away from the sufferers. The same suffix continues the chain from {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) and {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}), but the preposition reverses spatial logic. The result is a trap from both sides: no verdict comes upon them to end it, and no burden lifts away from them to ease it.

topics.headline: relief as removal denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees mitigation as something that would lift away from them, then sees that movement blocked.
topics.reason: The away-from phrase complements the lightening verb.

topics.headline: same group in reversed direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the identical plural target through opposite prepositional directions.
topics.reason: The suffix matches earlier phrases while the preposition changes from upon to away-from.

topics.headline: bound removal target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears denied removal and its target compressed in one surface word.
topics.reason: The preposition and suffix are fused.

words.gloss_range: partitive/source preposition under negation denying any portion of punishment being reduced
words.prose: {{ar:مِّنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) redirects the mitigation clause from the sufferers to the substance of torment. Under negated {{ar:يُخَفَّفُ}} ({{tr:yukhaffafu}}), it works partitively: not any portion of {{ar:عَذَابِهَا}} ({{tr:ʿadhābihā}}) is reduced. Its strengthened recitational entry after {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) keeps the punishment portion from sounding like an afterthought.

topics.headline: no portion reduced
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial reaches any part of the punishment, not only the whole.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the punishment noun after a negated mitigation verb.

topics.headline: source and partitive pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees both no relief from the punishment and no reduction of any portion of it.
topics.reason: The local prepositional frame supports source/partitive readings under negation.

topics.headline: audible bridge to punishment phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the removal phrase and punishment phrase tightened together.
topics.reason: Phonetic rows mark the contact between the preceding pronoun phrase and the preposition.

words.gloss_range: fire-domain-owned punishment treated as divisible burden but not reduced
words.root_gloss_range: sweet/freshness and torment branches; local fire and mitigation context selects torment while making sweetness/easing the absent counter-pole
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابِهَا}} ({{tr:ʿadhābihā}}) names the burden that {{ar:يُخَفَّفُ}} ({{tr:yukhaffafu}}) would reduce, and the feminine suffix binds it back to the {{ar:نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ}} ({{tr:nāru jahannama}}) domain. The noun is abstract, but {{ar:مِّنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes it behave like a divisible load so that even partial relief can be denied. The ʿ-dh-b sweetness branch is narrowed out locally; in this fire-domain the payoff is torment with the sweet or easing pole absent (35:12). Formulaically, this returns severe punishment from 35:7 and no-lightening language such as 2:86, but with the local suffix keeping the torment tied to this fire-domain.

topics.headline: punishment owned by fire-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the torment as belonging to the named fire-domain, not as a detachable penalty.
topics.reason: The feminine suffix points back to the fire/Jahannam domain complex.

topics.headline: abstract burden made divisible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that torment is grammatically treated as a measurable load so no portion can be lightened.
topics.reason: The genitive noun after partitive preposition supplies the material of denied mitigation.

topics.headline: torment branch over sweetness branch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the root's sweet-water pole become an absent relief against the selected punishment sense, especially beside 35:12.
topics.reason: Root evidence includes sweetness and torment, but fire, Jahannam, and lightening select the torment branch.

words.gloss_range: prefixed comparative/modal kāf turning the prior scene into the manner of recompense
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) begins {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:kadhālika}}) and makes the preceding no-exit scene the manner of recompense. The comparison is not decorative: the described pattern of fire, non-death, and non-lightening is exactly the mode by which {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) operates. The bound kāf compresses likeness, manner, and backward reference into the closing formula.

topics.headline: prior scene as manner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment just described become the mode of recompense, not a loose simile.
topics.reason: The prefixed comparative preposition governs the demonstrative and modifies the recompense clause.

topics.headline: bound comparison to pointer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices comparison and deictic reference fused in one formulaic phrase.
topics.reason: The particle is prefixed to the demonstrative.

topics.headline: hinge from scene to rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verse pivot from described punishment to administered principle.
topics.reason: Discourse rows identify the phrase as the hinge into the closing recompense rule.

words.gloss_range: demonstrative pointer gathering the whole prior punishment pattern
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) points back to the whole architecture, not only the nearest noun. Fire, denied death, and denied mitigation become one deictic object that {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) can apply as a rule. The distal form makes the just-described scene stand back as a complete pattern ready for generalization.

topics.headline: demonstrative governed by kāf
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the pointer as part of a modal phrase rather than a free-floating pronoun.
topics.reason: The demonstrative is governed by the prefixed comparative preposition.

topics.headline: whole scene gathered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entire no-exit pattern is being summarized, not just fire or punishment alone.
topics.reason: The demonstrative definitizes the preceding described pattern.

topics.headline: clasp before final rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the pointer clasp the scene before the active recompense verb universalizes it.
topics.reason: Structural rows make the demonstrative the transition into the final rule statement.

words.gloss_range: active first-person plural recompense verb converting passive punishment into administered return
words.root_gloss_range: rewarding, punishing, settling accounts, and giving what is due; local phrase selects punitive matched recompense
words.prose: {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) reintroduces active agency after the passive suffering clauses. In the standard reading it takes {{ar:كُلَّ كَفُورٍۢ}} ({{tr:kulla kafūrin}}) as object, so the no-exit state is not impersonal mechanics but administered recompense. The j-z-y account-settling field is narrowed by {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:kadhālika}}) to punitive matched return; the fitting-recompense idea is explicit in 78:26, while here the fit is no completed death and no mitigation for the intensified denier. The variants around active/passive voice expose how important agency is at this closing verb.

topics.headline: active agency after passives
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the passive punishment states resolved as directly administered recompense.
topics.reason: The active first-person plural imperfect follows two passive clauses and governs the object phrase.

topics.headline: punitive matched return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the account-settling logic of recompense, while reward-side uses of the root are not locally selected.
topics.reason: Root evidence allows reward and penalty; the prior no-exit scene selects punitive requital.

topics.headline: closing rule with voice pressure

words.gloss_range: accusative construct totality distributing recompense across every instance of the class
words.root_gloss_range: totality, completeness, encompassing, and other branches such as weariness; local quantifier selects exhaustive coverage
words.prose: {{ar:كُلَّ}} ({{tr:kulla}}) heads the object phrase after {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) in the standard reading and governs {{ar:كَفُورٍۢ}} ({{tr:kafūrin}}) as its genitive class complement. The passive variant makes the same word nominative subject, showing how voice would reroute the final grammar; the standard active form keeps it as object head. The singular quantifier with a singular indefinite type does not shrink the scope; it distributes recompense across every instance and turns one group's fate into a class-wide rule. This reverses the universal death frame of 3:185 by universalizing recompense while death is denied. Its totality sense is local, while other k-l-l branches such as weariness are not active here.

words.prose: {{ar:كَفُورٍۢ}} ({{tr:kafūrin}}) closes the ayah on the culprit type, not on the fire. As the genitive complement of {{ar:كُلَّ}} ({{tr:kulla}}), its indefinite singular form leaves the class open to every instance, while the faʿūl pattern marks habitual, deepened denial or ingratitude rather than one isolated act. The covering image has hardened into an enclosing disposition, and the gratitude/kafūr binary in 76:3 supplies the punitive side here. The final k-f-r root returns to {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) and turns the opening deed into a settled character category whose recompense is the no-exit middle of the ayah.

topics.headline: last word as moral key

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The first negation joins a denied decisive act to death, while the second independently denies any reduction of the punishment.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verse closes both ways in which the condition could change: decisive completion through death and quantitative modulation through relief. Continued existence is therefore structured as non-termination plus non-reduction, not merely as a long duration.

activation_trace.role: The root's death-enacting verdict sense supplies the terminal event explicitly blocked by the first negation.
Its completion and expiry sense broadens the denied event from dying to reaching an endpoint at all.
Loss of life is the unavailable terminal release rather than the punishment's ordinary result.
Lightening a weight supplies the second possible state-change, whose negation leaves the load undiminished.
Severe painful punishment identifies what persists when neither endpoint nor easing is admitted.

changed_reading.before: The verse says that the punishment lasts forever.
changed_reading.after: The verse designs a suspended condition with two separately barred transitions: it cannot complete in death and cannot vary downward in intensity.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated unbelief root encloses the fire clause and returns in the final universal object of recompense.
baseline_models.mechanism: A covering or concealment action is answered by a fire-root whose inventory also carries illumination and visible marking. The focus can therefore hold an exposure reversal: what was covered is met by a medium that both burns and makes manifest.

activation_trace.role: Literal covering supplies the action that the fire can reverse by disclosure.
Concealment or rejection of truth keeps the covering image anchored in the verse's human designation.
Actual burning fire supplies the punitive medium and its agitated visible action.
The same inventory's illumination sense lets the fire function as exposure without replacing its literal heat.

changed_reading.before: Fire is only the instrument that burns the unbelievers.
changed_reading.after: Fire remains literal punishment but also reverses concealment, forcing visibility where truth or benefit had been covered.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The concluding comparison joins recompense to every emphatically characterized ingrate, while the same root also opens the verse.
baseline_models.mechanism: The closing clause turns the preceding no-exit mechanism into a rule of responsive consequence. Comprehensive scope and repeated ingratitude make the case neither accidental nor merely collective: each complete instance of the stance falls under the response.

activation_trace.role: Countering an act with its consequence supplies the responsive link between the stance and the described condition.
Comprehensive inclusion distributes the rule across the whole class without leaving an unaddressed part.
Denial of benefit or failure to acknowledge it specifies the recurring disposition answered by the recompense.

changed_reading.before: A named group receives a generic sentence.
changed_reading.after: The no-exit condition is presented as a comprehensive response to each fully formed instance of unacknowledged benefit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier opening-and-holding pair describes controlled access to mercy: what is opened cannot be detained, and what is detained cannot be sent onward. Against that system, the focus occupies a release-disabled state in which neither the terminal channel of death nor the lesser channel of easing opens.

activation_trace.role: Completion is the focus's blocked terminal channel.
Reduction of a load is the focus's blocked partial-release channel.
An opened closure and widened entry supply the positive gate operation against which the focus reads as shut.
Tender mercy identifies what flows through the open side of the control pair.
Holding and confining supply the opposing operation and make continued detention a live mechanism.
Sending onward supplies the release operation absent from the focus condition.

structural_cues: 35:2 and 35:36 both use paired clauses to exhaust complementary control possibilities.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opening, detention, and dispatch; I treat death and easing as two release channels. A live alternative is a simpler moral contrast between mercy and punishment without a shared gate mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The two negations merely intensify duration and pain.
changed_reading.after: The two negations specify a controlled detention in which both full release and partial relief are disabled.

context_deltas.mechanism: Elsewhere in the packet, death is a hinge in a dead-earth-to-life sequence, moving things run toward an appointed limit, and worldly people are deferred only until their term. The focus's denied death can therefore mean more than endless biological survival: the normal hinge into another phase is withheld after the ordinary clock has already done its work.

activation_trace.role: Loss of life is the focus transition explicitly made unavailable.
Lifeless land supplies a material death-state that is subsequently crossed rather than treated as a final stop.
Earth restored by rain supplies the next phase on the far side of the death-state.
Revival after death makes the transition model explicit rather than merely botanical.
Continuous running supplies ordinary movement toward a temporal boundary.
A fixed terminal time supplies the normal goal toward which the running proceeds.
Deferral to a later time distinguishes temporary worldly postponement from the focus's post-term non-completion.
The twice-marked term confirms that ordinary delay still reaches a boundary, sharpening the focus's missing endpoint.

structural_cues: The packet uses the same analogical formula after revived land and after the focus punishment, inviting comparison of two opposite transition patterns.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reversible death, goal-directed time, and bounded deferral; I infer that denied death withholds a phase transition. The live alternative is that these passages establish duration only, without making death itself a beneficial hinge.

changed_reading.before: Not dying means simply remaining alive under punishment.
changed_reading.after: Not dying also means being denied the transition that death elsewhere mediates, in a condition no longer moving toward an appointed endpoint.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier burden rule denies transfer even when a heavily loaded person calls for help. That exact heavy-versus-light field changes the focus's non-lightening into personal non-delegability: the recompensed load cannot be shifted, shared, or carried away by another.

activation_trace.role: Lightness opposed to weight makes relief measurable as removal of load.
Act-responsive recompense attaches the unreduced load to the conduct it answers.
Comprehensive scope applies the non-transfer rule to each member covered by the closing clause.
A personally borne heavy load supplies the object that another bearer cannot remove.
Weight as the direct opposite of lightness locks the earlier burden clause to the focus's relief verb.
Bearing responsibility or burden supplies the attempted transfer that the packet explicitly refuses.

structural_cues: 35:18 says that none of the called person's load is carried away, while 35:36 says none of the punishment is lightened away from them.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a non-transferable heavy load and the focus supplies non-lightening; I map the legal burden rule onto punishment relief. The alternative is that 35:18 concerns responsibility before judgment and does not describe the later experience.

changed_reading.before: No lightening means only that the intensity remains high.
changed_reading.after: No lightening also means that each person's consequence is non-transferable: no other bearer can take off even part of the load.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet moves from beautified wrongdoing mis-seen as good, through the contrast of darkness and light, to an illuminating book followed by the taking of those who rejected. This sequence strengthens the focus fire as belated clarification: the same root field that provides literal flame now makes prior concealment and distorted seeing impossible.

activation_trace.role: Rejection or concealment of truth supplies the epistemic condition reversed by exposure.
Literal flame keeps the exposure model anchored in the actual focus punishment.
Making something appear attractive supplies the cosmetic layer that distorts judgment.
Seeing by eye or insight supplies the faculty whose evaluation has been misdirected.
Illumination set against darkness makes disclosure a packet-level contrast, not a focus-only wordplay.
The illuminating book supplies an earlier, non-punitive opportunity for clarification.
Rejection immediately after the illuminating book connects refused clarification to the focus's later fiery clarification.

structural_cues: The visual sequence runs from mis-seeing, to darkness/light, to an illuminating book, to rejection, and finally to fire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies distorted seeing, light, an illuminating book, rejection, and literal fire; I infer that the fire functions as forced disclosure. The alternative is that the shared root field is incidental and the fire has no epistemic role.

changed_reading.before: The fire only inflicts bodily pain after rejection.
changed_reading.after: The fire also becomes a terminal mode of seeing: refused illumination returns as inescapable exposure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet describes favorable response as full payment without deficiency and then an added gift, while repeatedly characterizing the giver through appreciative return. The focus answers the opposite disposition with recompense that is not reduced. The economy is responsive but not flatly symmetrical: acknowledgment receives completion plus surplus, whereas ingratitude receives an unreduced consequence.

activation_trace.role: Response to an act provides the common accounting relation across favorable and punitive outcomes.
Reduction in amount is explicitly denied on the punitive side of the comparison.
Failure to acknowledge benefit identifies the stance answered on the punitive side.
Full completion without deficiency supplies the baseline favorable payment.
Growth beyond the completed amount supplies the favorable surplus absent from the punitive side.
Gift or beneficence marks the increase as generosity rather than a debt mechanically owed.
Acknowledging benefit supplies the positive response pole against the focus's ingratitude pole.
The immediately preceding appreciative epithet brings that positive pole next to the focus's final ingrate designation.

structural_cues: The emphatic appreciative epithet immediately before the focus is answered by the emphatic ingrate epithet at the focus close.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies full payment, added gift, appreciation, ingratitude, and non-reduction; I infer a deliberately asymmetric response economy. The alternative is that the favorable surplus and punitive constancy are unrelated promises.

changed_reading.before: Recompense is a uniform one-for-one exchange.
changed_reading.after: Recompense is responsive but asymmetric: acknowledged benefit is met with fullness and surplus, while entrenched ingratitude is met with a consequence that receives no discount.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding residence is durable yet defined by removal of sorrow and non-contact with fatigue. The focus residence is also durable, but its durability is built by withholding terminal departure and withholding reduction. Permanence is therefore not the decisive value; what can leave, touch, or lessen within the permanent abode is.

activation_trace.role: Denied completion prevents the punitive residence from ending.
Denied lightening prevents painful weight from receding inside that residence.
Painful punishment names what remains present on the negative side of the paired residences.
Going away supplies the positive residence's removal operation.
Inner roughness from grief is the harmful state successfully removed there.
Settling in a place establishes the positive scene as a residence rather than a passing reward.
Stable staying supplies the permanence shared by the two neighboring outcomes.
Contact by an effect supplies the ingress explicitly denied to fatigue in the positive residence.
Exhausting toil supplies one harmful effect that cannot touch the positive residents.
Weakness and fatigue complete the double non-contact pattern mirrored by the focus's double negation.

structural_cues: 35:35 and 35:36 are adjacent residence descriptions, each closed by two coordinated negations.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies permanent settlement without harmful contact followed by fire without death or easing; I read them as deliberately paired architectures. The alternative is that adjacency contrasts outcomes generally without making their negation patterns formally reciprocal.

changed_reading.before: Paradise is permanent comfort and fire is permanent pain.
changed_reading.after: Both are durable residences, but one continually excludes harmful contact while the other continually excludes both departure and diminution; permanence itself is morally neutral until its internal traffic is specified.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet earlier associates the dead in graves with being beyond human address, but immediately after the focus the occupants remain vocally urgent, experientially responsive, and capable of requesting exit. Denied death thus preserves sentience and appeal while denying both escape and effective aid.

activation_trace.role: The unavailable loss of life leaves the occupants on the responsive side of the packet's living/dead contrast.
Painful experience is what continued responsiveness keeps perceptible.
Making another hear supplies the communicative capacity denied to the grave-side comparison.
Burial of the dead locates the packet's image of communicative unreachability.
A loud appeal for rescue demonstrates active voice and social need after death has been denied.
Passage to an outside supplies the exit they consciously request but do not receive.
Direct experiential testing confirms retained perception rather than mere biological persistence.
Aid and vindication supply the social response explicitly unavailable to their appeal.

structural_cues: 35:22 places the dead beyond address; 35:36 denies death; 35:37 immediately displays crying, requesting, and tasting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies communicative unreachability for the dead and vivid perception for the fire's occupants; I infer that denied death enforces sentience. The alternative is that the later speech and tasting are conventional scene details with no special relation to the death negation.

changed_reading.before: Not dying is only the absence of a bodily endpoint.
changed_reading.after: Not dying also preserves the very capacities by which the punishment is perceived and escape is desired: voice, experience, and unanswered appeal.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later context depicts created order as actively held from leaving its state and then denies both substitution and transformation in the governing pattern. Those controls sharpen the focus's double blockage into active conservation: the punishment is maintained against terminal removal and internal reduction rather than simply continuing by inertia.

activation_trace.role: Completion or expiry is the first state-change prevented in the focus.
Reduction of weight is the second state-change prevented in the focus.
Active holding and confinement supply the conserving force rather than passive duration.
Departure from a place or condition supplies the change that active holding prevents.
Substitution of one thing for another supplies a replacement route denied by the stable pattern.
Transformation away from a condition supplies the internal change route likewise denied.

structural_cues: The focus denies two state changes; 35:41 and 35:43 later pair holding against removal with no substitution and no transformation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies active cosmic holding and invariant non-substitution; I extend that control pattern to the focus's two denied transitions. The alternative is that the later verses concern cosmic order and historical regularity without describing the maintenance of punishment.

changed_reading.before: The punishment persists because nothing happens to end it.
changed_reading.after: The punishment can be read as actively conserved: removal, replacement, transformation, and quantitative easing are all controlled away.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later clauses place each person's rejection upon that person, make it accumulate as loss, and state that harmful scheming descends around its own people. These cues turn the focus's assignment and recompense into a feedback enclosure: the consequence is not only externally imposed but adheres to, grows from, and closes around the stance it answers.

activation_trace.role: Entrenched non-acknowledgment supplies the stance whose effects return to its bearer.
Responsive consequence supplies the return path from conduct to condition.
Comprehensive scope closes the rule around every complete instance of the stance.
Repeated ingratitude placed upon its own bearer supplies the self-attaching part of the feedback loop.
Increase and growth make the attached consequence cumulative rather than static.
General diminution identifies the accumulating result as loss to the bearer.
Harm descending and surrounding supplies the spatial closure of the feedback mechanism.
A group defined by belonging identifies the scheme's own people as the enclosure's recipients.

structural_cues: The focus cycles through assignment to them, action upon them, no removal from them, and universal recompense; 35:39 and 35:43 make that return-to-agent pattern explicit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies self-borne rejection, increasing loss, and harm enclosing its own people; I combine them into a feedback loop around the focus's prepositions. The alternative is that these are separate accountability formulas without a single spatial-causal mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Fire is an external penalty assigned by a judge.
changed_reading.after: Fire can also be read as a self-adhering and accumulating consequence that closes around the very disposition to which it responds.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the focus recompense root's non-dominant cutting inventory together with the unbelief root's agricultural branch. It remains anchored in two supplied focus mappings and is made materially live by the packet's ripe-fruit cue. Downstream prose should present it only as a branch-level harvest image, never as the lexical translation of the clause or as a replacement for moral recompense.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The final recompense verb, the comprehensive quantifier, and the repeated unbelief root permit a secondary image of a complete harvest reaching its cutting point.

activation_trace.role: Ordinary act-responsive recompense remains the controlling sense that contains the agricultural image.
A crop or fleece reaching the time for cutting supplies the non-dominant harvest endpoint.
Covering seed in soil supplies the agricultural actor image linked to the focus designation.
Completeness makes the image a whole harvest rather than an isolated cutting.
Ripe fruit makes maturation-to-harvest a visible packet image instead of an inventory-only pun.

changed_reading.before: Recompense is only an abstract juridical return.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the comprehensive recompense also carries a harvest-at-ripeness image: the seed-covering stance reaches the point at which its grown consequence is cut.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it lets the punishment root's neighboring sweetness, abstention, and prevention branches interact with an earlier use of the same QAC root for fresh water. It remains valid as a material analogy anchored in the focus punishment, fire, and non-lightening, with later tasting confirming experience. Downstream prose should call it an inversion of refreshment, not claim that punishment etymologically means sweet water.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The punishment noun stands beside fire and an explicit denial of relief, allowing its wider supplied branch field to model deprivation as well as inflicted pain.

activation_trace.role: Severe pain and punishment remain the direct focus sense that contains the analogy.
Prevention or weaning away supplies deprivation as one functional component of the painful condition.
The denied removal of weight makes unavailable refreshment operate as unrelieved load.
Literal fire gives the denied-refreshment image its material pressure.
Fresh pleasant water activates the positive sensory pole carried by the same supplied root inventory.
Exceptionally fresh water intensifies the refreshment pole that the focus reverses.
Easy passage through the throat makes palatability and bodily relief concrete.
Taking in liquid completes the packet's positive refreshment mechanism.
Direct experience or testing makes the later punitive condition sensory rather than merely abstract.

changed_reading.before: Punishment is only positive infliction of pain.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, punishment also appears as anti-refreshment: fire-bound experience in which sweetness, easy intake, and the easing they imply are continually withheld.

strongest_changes: The paired negations became a two-channel control mechanism barring both terminal release and partial relief.
The non-lightening became a non-transferable personal load when read against the burden rule of 35:18.
The adjacent permanent abodes became inverses: one excludes harmful contact, while the other excludes departure and diminution.
The fire acquired a plausible disclosure function through the packet's sequence of distorted seeing, light, illuminating text, rejection, and flame.
Denied death became enforced sentience and a withheld transition, not merely endless biological survival.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly changed static duration into controlled process: opening versus holding, death as a transition hinge, burden that cannot transfer, residence defined by what may enter or leave, and consequence that grows around its bearer. Split focus mappings also preserved two high-risk but anchored material images, harvest and anti-refreshment.
remaining_uncertainties: The transition-hinge model depends on carrying the dead-earth revival sequence into the post-judgment scene; duration alone remains a live reading.
The disclosure function of fire is supported by the shared root and visual sequence but may remain secondary to literal punishment.
Active conservation and self-enclosure are reader-supplied causal syntheses rather than explicit directional claims in a single clause.
The harvest and anti-refreshment readings must remain exploratory branch images and must not be rendered as lexical translations.

baseline.text: İnkâr edenler için cehennem ateşi vardır. Ölümlerine hükmedilmez ki ölsünler; ateşin azabı da onlardan hafifletilmez. Her nankörü işte böyle cezalandırırız.

findings.text: Azabın sürekliliği, hem sonlandıran ölümün hem de yükü kısmen azaltan hafiflemenin ayrı ayrı kapatılmasıyla etkin biçimde korunur.
Nankörlüğün karşılığı, kendisine ulaşan nimeti örtmenin karşısında ona denk düşen olumsuz bir hesaplaşma olarak kurulur.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P3 (35:31-45) Fire, Death, and Failed Exit
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Punishment becomes a closed process when fire persists, death is withheld as an endpoint, relief is denied, and cries fail to establish an exit relation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Legal completion, sensory tasting, aid, and spatial exit separate several ways an ordeal might terminate and show each one failing independently.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Fire without terminal death
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Fire is experienced as punishment, but the decree that would complete life is withheld and the burden of the ordeal is not reduced.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: consuming fire (quranic:root_001564:B002/m01); decree brought to completion (quranic:root_001237:B003/m01); completion or expiration of a term (quranic:root_001237:B004/m01); loss of life (quranic:root_001454:B001/m01); experiential tasting (quranic:root_000526:B002/m01); painful punishment (quranic:root_000994:B005/m01); reduction of a burden (quranic:root_000427:B001/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 35:36 `نَارُ/يُقْضَىٰ/يَمُوتُ/يُخَفَّفُ/عَذَابِ` (ن و ر/ق ض ي/م و ت/خ ف ف/ع ذ ب); 35:37 `ذُوقُ` (ذ و ق).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Death, expiration, and lightening are distinct terminal operations. Their coordinated refusal creates persistence: the fire continues, the sufferer remains alive to experience it, and intensity is not reduced.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Intended action accrues to its agent and returns as a consequence that can increase rank or compound loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Commerce, growth, precedence, and earned acquisition make consequence cumulative and agent-bound rather than a single externally imposed event.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Action acquired and returned
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An agent intentionally performs an act, acquires it as part of the self's account, and meets the consequence that follows it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: intentional action (quranic:root_001046:B001/m01); recompense according to deed (quranic:root_000244:B001/m01); acquisition by one's act (quranic:root_001296:B001/m01); consequence or final outcome (quranic:root_001033:B006/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The sequence preserves agency at every stage: intention produces an act, the act is acquired to its performer, and recompense is the act's returned outcome rather than an unrelated imposition.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi nimeti yadsımayı, onu örtmeyi ve gereği olan şükrü yerine getirmemeyi aynı çekirdekte birleştirir; dalın geçici çerçevesi bu koşulu doğru yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Nesne özellikle nimettir ve belirleyici sonuç şükrün terkidir; genel dinî ret bu dala kendiliğinden girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Nimeti yadsıma çekirdeği yalın ve türemiş kullanımlarda korunur; nimetle kurulan yapı ve aşırılık bildiren kişi nitelemesi ayrı gerçekleşmelerdir.

concept_map.definition: Bir nimeti tanımamak, değerini örtmek veya onun gerektirdiği şükrü yerine getirmemektir. Bu tutumda aşırı olan kişi de aynı anlam alanında nitelenir.

facets.statement: Bir nimeti yadsıma veya şükrünü yerine getirmeyerek değerini örtme.
Nimetleri sürekli ve aşırı biçimde yadsıyan kişi bu tutumun yoğunlaşmış taşıyıcısıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar nimeti yadsımayı şükrün karşıtı sayar; örtme açıklaması, nimetin gerektirdiği şükrü yerine getirmemeyi bu karşıtlığın belirleyici davranışı yapar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Nimeti tanımama ile ona şükretmeme çekirdeğini kısa ve doğal biçimde verir.

error_profile.preserves: Nimetin inkâr edilmesini ve şükrün terk edilmesini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir nimetin veya yapılan iyiliğin tanınmadığı gündelik bağlamlarda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Yapılan iyiliği tanımama ve karşılığında şükretmeme tutumunu korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: nimeti yadsımak ve şükrünü yerine getirmemek
iyilikleri karşılıksız ve teşekkürsüz kalan cömert adam

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal nimeti tanımamayı ve şükrünü terk etmeyi bildirir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sözün bir şeyden uzak olduğunu bildirme, onunla bağını reddetme ve ondan sıyrılma anlamında kullanılabildiğini açıkça söyler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal bir inancı yadsımak değil, belirli bir şeyle bağı reddedip ondan uzaklaşmaktır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca bir şeyden uzaklaşmayı bildiren bağlı yapıda korunur; yalın köke genel bir ayrılma anlamı verilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyle olan bağı reddetmek, ondan uzak olduğunu açıklamak ve sorumluluk ya da aidiyet bağından sıyrılmaktır.

facets.statement: Belirli bir şeyle bağı reddederek ondan uzaklaşma ve kendini onun dışında tutma.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bağlı kullanımın bir şeyden uzak olduğunu ilan etme ve onunla ilişkiden sıyrılma anlamı taşıdığında birleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişi, görüş, eylem veya sorumlulukla ilişkiyi açıkça reddeden bağlı kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Bağı reddetme ile o bağdan uzaklaşma işlemlerini birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir kişi veya şeyle ilişkiyi reddetme ve ondan uzak durma iki dalda ortaktır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yapısal olarak bağlı ve dar bir ilişki reddidir; komşu dal genel uzaklık, arınmışlık ve sorumsuzluk bildirimlerini de içerir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel bağ kesme ve uzak durma dalı en yakın anlam sınırını verdiği için yayımlandı.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Eylem kişinin kendi reddi değil, başka bir kişinin durumu hakkında adlandırma veya hüküm vermedir.

İşlemin sonucu, kötülüğün işlenmemiş gibi değerlendirilmesi veya etkisinin silinmesidir.
